name: Employer/Employee Work Permit (Quota System)

requirements.blocker_text: The government sets yearly foreign-worker hiring quotas by industry and region (including Bishkek); an unused quota allocation lapses after 3 months. The employer must obtain an Employment Permit (~$58) and the foreign worker (18+) an Employee Permit (~$29); entrepreneurs pay ~$291. Permits are typically issued for 1 year with annual renewal, are employer-specific and non-transferable, and can be refused or revoked if a qualified local candidate exists, submitted data is inaccurate, employment ends, or illegal conduct occurs. Citizens of EEU member states (Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Armenia) have been exempt from this system since August 2015, as are recognized refugees/asylees, permanent residents, and ethnic Kyrgyz returnees.
requirements.fix_path: Secure employer sponsorship within the applicable regional/industry quota, and obtain both the Employment Permit (employer) and Employee Permit (worker).

evidence_required.document: Employer Employment Permit and worker Employee Permit within the annual quota

outcome.duration_length: 1 year, renewable annually (2 years for some skilled workers, up to 3 for entrepreneurs, per the source, though it notes 1-year permits are issued 'irrespective of position or qualification' in practice)

sources.title: Kalikova & Associates (law firm) -- employment of foreigners in the Kyrgyz Republic: quota system, Employment/Employee Permits, EEU exemption, fees
